subject: Action required: EU / US / APAC traffic reroute + audit info
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@finco.io>, ops@acme-payments.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Action required: EU / US / APAC traffic reroute + audit info

Hi Alice / FinCo ops team —

Quick summary up front: between ~07:45–08:10 PT today we observed elevated error rates and regional timeouts affecting requests routed to two cloud provider regions (us-east1 and eu-west1). CloudProvider acknowledges a control-plane incident that temporarily impacted outbound networking for certain AZs; status link below.

What Redwood did automatically:
- Immediate policy: we switched affected customers to our cross-region fallback pool (automatic reroute) to keep successful requests flowing. For most traffic we saw recovery within 3–5 minutes after fallback routing.
- We throttled retries to avoid amplification and surfaced 502/504s to SDKs while failover window completed.

Immediate action we recommend for FinCo (steps attached in reroute-checklist.pdf):
1) If you have a region pin in your SDK, switch to the global routing policy ("regional_preference: auto") or set explicit fallbacks to an unaffected region (apac-south1 / us-west2).
2) For DNS customers using CNAME to region-endpoints: add the provided global-cname.redwood.ai entry with a low TTL (60s) during the incident window.
3) If you require strict regional isolation, open the attached checklist and coordinate with me — we can provision a temporary dedicated route via our Dedicated pool.

Attached: reroute-checklist.pdf (short checklist + config snippets).

We are compiling a limited audit sample of request logs and will share an anonymized CSV slice for your SOC/compliance review (expected in ~45 minutes). If you need export of request-level evidence for an audit, tell me the timeframe and we'll prioritize.

Short answers to likely questions:
- Was customer data exfiltrated? No indication of any data leakage; services that store or log data were not modified during the failover.
- Will this affect billing? We'll run a usage/credit evaluation once the postmortem is complete — Sergio is looped for commercial/remedy.

Status and links:
- CloudProvider status: https://status.cloudprovider.example/incidents/2027-03-22-region-outage
- Internal ticket: INC-5541 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-5541)

I will follow up with the audit slice and an engineering note from Evelyn with precise failure signatures. If you'd like a 30-minute bridge to walk through the logs now, we can set one up.

— Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
(attachment: reroute-checklist.pdf (PDF, 48KB))

Hi Alice / Monica —

Attached is a small anonymized audit sample covering 07:30–08:45 PT (audit-sample-20270322.csv). Fields: request_id, ts_utc, route_region, http_status, retry_count, latency_ms. We removed any sensitive payload fields — there are no raw customer payloads in the CSV. If you need additional columns (headers, request hashes), tell me which keys and we'll redact appropriately.

Technical notes (short):
- Root signature: control-plane networking update at CloudProvider triggered BGP flap across two AZs in us-east1 and eu-west1; packet loss manifested as connection resets and 5xx from the upstream edge.
- Redwood behavior: our routing policy detected elevated loss and flipped to cross-region fallback pools; KV cache warm-up caused a temporary latency spike for some long-running chat sessions.
- Mitigation applied: adjusted retry backoff window and expanded cross-region pool capacity by 20% to absorb burst traffic.

SDK config snippet to force global fallback immediately:
- header: X-Redwood-Routing: global-fallback
- set regional_preference: auto in client config (example attached in reroute-checklist.pdf)

We will append full request logs to the INC ticket and provide redacted request traces on request.

— Evelyn

Subject: RE: Action required: EU / US / APAC traffic reroute + audit info — postmortem & next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for the quick responses yesterday. This is a short post-incident summary and next steps. Full postmortem is linked below.

Summary of cause:
- CloudProvider control-plane instability triggered transient network disruptions in two regions (us-east1, eu-west1). The issue caused packet loss and short-lived connection resets at the edge, producing 502/504 errors for some customers pinned to those regions.

What we did and what we will do (actions):
1) Auto-failover: our routing policies switched traffic to cross-region pools within 30–90s for affected customers.
2) Durable mitigation: we updated our failover window and increased cross-region pool capacity; this is already rolled to production.
3) Preventive: we are adding an extra health-check layer and will default new customer projects to a conservative global-fallback unless region isolation is explicitly requested.
4) Compliance: we have provided an anonymized audit sample (attached) and will deliver a full redacted log export on request for your auditors.

Commercial remedy: Sergio will follow up on a credit proposal. We are offering an interim one-time credit for measurable impact windows and will finalize after the root cause report.

SLA / timeline: postmortem doc (drive link) will include timelines, affected customer count, and RCA. Expect the full postmortem by EOD tomorrow.

Link to postmortem: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cReroutePostmortem
Internal ticket: INC-5541: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-5541
CloudProvider incident: https://status.cloudprovider.example/incidents/2027-03-22-region-outage

If you'd like a call, I have availability tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PT. We'll also share a short guidance doc for customers who intentionally want single-region isolation and how to avoid unexpected failovers.

Thanks — we appreciate your partnership and will keep you updated.

— Monica
